proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(x\) and suppress its subscript.  A selected--selected coupling is an array
\(\gamma=(\gamma_{ij})_{i,j\in\mathcal Y}\) such that
\[
 \gamma_{ij}\geq 0,\qquad
 \sum_j\gamma_{ij}\leq u_i,\qquad
 \sum_i\gamma_{ij}\leq v_j,\qquad
 \sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij}=h.
\]
Its benefit mass is \(n(\gamma)=\sum_{j>i}\gamma_{ij}\).

We first establish the required ordered partial-matching capacities directly by a residual-network argument.  For the benefit graph, join row \(i\) to column \(j\) exactly when \(j>i\), put capacities \(u_i\) and \(v_j\) on the source and sink arcs, and give every row--column arc capacity larger than \(U+V\).  A maximum flow exists because the feasible-flow set is compact.  If its residual graph contained a source-to-sink path, increasing the flow by the smallest positive residual capacity on that path would contradict maximality.  Hence the vertices reachable from the source define a cut whose capacity equals the flow value: every forward arc crossing this cut is saturated and every backward arc crossing it carries zero flow, so summing flow conservation over the source side gives this equality.

It remains to inspect such cuts.  If the source-side row set is empty, the cut has capacity \(U\), which is \(G_K\).  Otherwise let \(k\) be its smallest row index.  Finiteness of the cut forces all columns \(j>k\) onto the source side.  Adding every row \(i\geq k\) and deleting every other source-side column can only decrease its capacity.  The resulting threshold cut has capacity
\[
 \sum_{i<k}u_i+\sum_{j>k}v_j=G_k.
\]
Thus the maximum mass of a benefit-only partial matching is
\[
 G^star:=\min_{0\leq k\leq K}G_k.
\]
Applying the same argument to the nonbenefit graph \(j\leq i\), a nonempty source-side row set can be replaced by the initial segment ending at its largest index \(k\).  Its threshold-cut capacity is
\[
 \sum_{i>k}u_i+\sum_{j\leq k}v_j=B_k,
\]
while the empty row set gives \(B_{-1}=U\).  Therefore the maximum nonbenefit-only mass is
\[
 B^star:=\min_{-1\leq k\leq K-1}B_k.
\]
This is the finite capacitated cut technique, with both the cut equality and the reduction to threshold cuts derived above rather than assumed.

To minimize benefit in a coupling of total mass \(h\), take a maximum nonbenefit matching.  If \(h\leq B^star\), scaling that matching by \(h/B^star\) (with the zero case immediate) gives benefit zero.  If \(h>B^star\), maximality implies that every pair consisting of a residual positive-capacity row and a residual positive-capacity column is a benefit edge; otherwise one more nonbenefit edge could be added.  The residual row and column totals are \(U-B^star\) and \(V-B^star\), both at least \(h-B^star\) because \(h\leq\min\{U,V\}\).  A greedy coupling of residual rows and columns therefore adds benefit mass \(h-B^star\).  Consequently the minimum is
\[
 n_{min}=\max\{0,h-B^star\}.
\]
Interchanging benefit and nonbenefit gives, by the identical residual-capacity argument,
\[
 n_{max}=\min\{h,G^star\}.
\]
Convex combinations of the two attaining couplings preserve the row-capacity inequalities, column-capacity inequalities, and total mass \(h\), while their benefit masses fill every point of \([n_{min},n_{max}]\).  Since a maximum is bounded by each threshold cut, these endpoint formulas are equivalent to
\[
 0\leq n\leq h,\qquad n\geq h-B_k\quad(-1\leq k\leq K-1),
 \qquad n\leq G_k\quad(0\leq k\leq K).
\]

Finally, the selected--selected table is completed to the full complier table as follows.  Put its unused selected row mass \(u_i-\sum_j\gamma_{ij}\) in cell \((i,\bot)\), its unused selected column mass \(v_j-\sum_i\gamma_{ij}\) in cell \((\bot,j)\), and put
\[
 c-U-V+h
\]
in cell \((\bot,\bot)\).  The assumed lower bound on \(h\) makes the last number nonnegative, and the assumed upper bounds make every unused margin nonnegative.  The resulting row and column masses are exactly \((u_w)_{w\in\mathcal V}\) and \((v_w)_{w\in\mathcal V}\).  This proves necessity, sufficiency, and completion.

Define the potential observed state under received treatment \(d\) by
\[
 \widetilde V_d=\begin{cases}Y_d,&S_d=1,\\ \bot,&S_d=0.\end{cases}
\]
This is only a proof intermediate.  By receipt consistency and the two exclusion and consistency restrictions, a unit with response vector \(R\) is observed at
\((D_0,\widetilde V_{D_0})\) under \(Z=0\) and at
\((D_1,\widetilde V_{D_1})\) under \(Z=1\).  Conditional randomization then identifies the two arm marginals from the same response-law distribution within each covariate cell.

For the forward projection, fix \(x\).  Represent each response type by an arc from its \(Z=0\) state to its \(Z=1\) state, with mass \(P(X=x,R=r)\).  If \(D_0=D_1=d\), exclusion gives the same state at both ends, so this is a diagonal arc.  Let its mass at state \((d,w)\) be \(d_{xdw}\).  Nonnegativity and the two arm marginals give
\[
 0\leq d_{xdw}\leq\min\{q^0_{xdw},q^1_{xdw}\}.
\]
The off-diagonal arcs from treatment zero to treatment one are exactly compliers, and their left and right margins are \(u_{xw}\) and \(v_{xw}\).  The reverse arcs are exactly defiers, with treatment-zero and treatment-one margins \(r_{xw}\) and \(s_{xw}\).  Subtracting the diagonal masses from the observed marginals gives precisely the four equations in \(\mathrm{def:diagonal\text{-}residuals}\).  Taking totals yields the displayed common masses \(c_x\) and \(f_x\).

Within the complier coupling, let \(h_x\) be the mass with both potential selection indicators one.  Its selected row and column totals are \(U_x\) and \(V_x\), so the four selection-type masses are
\[
 h_x,\qquad U_x-h_x,\qquad V_x-h_x,\qquad c_x-U_x-V_x+h_x.
\]
Their nonnegativity is equivalent to
\[
 \max\{0,U_x+V_x-c_x\}\leq h_x\leq\min\{U_x,V_x\}.
\]
The preceding ordinal-cuts lemma applied to the selected--selected block gives exactly the inequalities imposed on \(n_x\).  Moreover,
\[
 \min\{a_x,b_x\}=\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x.
\]
Choose \(o_x=1\) when \(U_x\leq V_x\), and \(o_x=0\) otherwise.  Then the branch budget is exactly the maintained minority budget.  The defier budget is already \(\sum_xf_x\leq\delta_D\).  Hence every compatible full law projects into at least one branch.

Conversely, take a full reduced array in a branch \(Q_o\).  For each \(x\), the ordinal-cuts lemma constructs a selected--selected complier table having total \(h_x\), benefit mass \(n_x\), and row and column masses bounded by the selected parts of \(u_x\) and \(v_x\).  Its missing-category completion from that lemma is a full coupling of \(u_x\) and \(v_x\), hence a complier arc table.  Because \(r_x\) and \(s_x\) are nonnegative vectors with the same total \(f_x\), a coupling exists: if \(f_x>0\), the product table \(s_{xw}r_{xw'}/f_x\) has the required two margins, while the zero table applies when \(f_x=0\).  This is the defier arc table.  Add the diagonal arcs of masses \(d_{xdw}\).

Every resulting arc determines a response type.  On a cross-treatment arc, its two endpoints specify \((S_0,Y_0)\) and \((S_1,Y_1)\), with an arbitrary value, say zero, assigned to \(Y_d\) whenever \(S_d=0\).  On a diagonal treatment-\(d\) arc, the observed endpoint specifies the treatment-\(d\) response and the other treatment response is filled arbitrarily.  Thus all response coordinates are defined, all masses are nonnegative, and the two arc marginals are exactly \(q^0\) and \(q^1\).  Sampling \(Z\) independently of \(R\) conditional on \(X\), at the observed strictly interior assignment propensity, supplies conditional randomization and overlap without changing those conditional arm marginals.  Receipt, selection, and outcome consistency and both exclusions hold by construction.

The branch inequality is sufficient for the actual minority restriction because, cell by cell,
\[
 \min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x
 \leq o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x.
\]
Summation and the branch budget therefore imply the maintained budget.  The defier mass is exactly \(\sum_xf_x\).  This proves the reverse lift and hence the stated equality after applying the same \((d,h,n)\)-projection to both sides.  In particular, if
\[
 \Theta_I^{\mathrm{causal}}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 :=\left\{\Pr_P(Y_1>Y_0\mid C,S_0=S_1=1):
 P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S),\ P\text{ induces }q,\ H(P)>0\right\},
\]
then the just-proved two directions, rather than a definition, establish
\[
 \Theta_I^{\mathrm{causal}}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]

For size, retain the \(O(mK)\) residual variables and introduce, in each cell,
\[
 P^u_{x0}=P^v_{x0}=0,\qquad
 P^u_{x,k+1}=P^u_{xk}+u_{xk},\qquad
 P^v_{x,k+1}=P^v_{xk}+v_{xk}.
\]
Then \(U_x=P^u_{xK}\), \(V_x=P^v_{xK}\), and
\[
 B_{xk}=U_x-P^u_{x,k+1}+P^v_{x,k+1},\qquad
 G_{xk}=P^u_{xk}+V_x-P^v_{x,k+1},
\]
with the stated endpoint conventions.  Each recurrence and cut has constant support.  All other restrictions have constant support per category except the two global budget rows.  Thus variables, rows, and nonzero coefficients are \(O(mK)\).  The coefficients are obtained from integers and the entries of \(q,\delta_D,\delta_S\) by field operations, and hence are rational for rational inputs.

Fix an orientation \(o\) and abbreviate its compact polytope by \(Q_o\).  Compactness follows directly from the diagonal upper bounds by \(q\), the residual equalities, and \(0\leq n_x\leq h_x\leq\min\{U_x,V_x\}\).  We first prove a denominator-safe polytope fact.  Every point of a compact polytope is a convex combination of its finitely many vertices: indeed, in the minimal face containing a nonvertex point, extend a line through that point to the two boundary points of the face and induct on face dimension.  Finiteness follows because a vertex is determined by a full-rank subset of the finite constraint list.

Write a point as \(z=\sum_j\alpha_jz^j\), where the \(z^j\) are vertices.  Since the branch restrictions imply \(0\leq N(z)\leq H(z)\), a vertex with \(H(z^j)=0\) also has \(N(z^j)=0\).  If \(H(z)>0\), then
\[
 \frac{N(z)}{H(z)}
 =\sum_{j:H(z^j)>0}
 \frac{\alpha_jH(z^j)}{H(z)}\frac{N(z^j)}{H(z^j)},
 \qquad
 \sum_{j:H(z^j)>0}\frac{\alpha_jH(z^j)}{H(z)}=1.
\]
Thus a positive-denominator branch has a positive-denominator vertex, and its smallest and largest ratios are attained at such vertices.  Conversely, mixing its two endpoint vertices gives a positive denominator and, by continuity of the displayed ratio along the segment, every intermediate value.  Each nonempty branch image is therefore an attained closed interval.  This argument is unaffected by a sequence with \(H\downarrow0\).

The normalized program is exact.  A point \(z\in Q_o\) with \(H(z)>0\) maps to
\[
 y=z/H(z),\qquad \lambda=1/H(z),
\]
and satisfies all of its constraints with objective \(N(z)/H(z)\).  Conversely, a normalized feasible pair cannot have \(\lambda=0\): the homogenized diagonal upper bounds then force every diagonal coordinate to zero; the homogenized residual equalities force \(u,v,r,s,c,f\) to zero; and \(h_x\leq U_x,V_x\) then forces \(H=0\), contradicting \(\eta y=1\).  Hence \(z=y/\lambda\in Q_o\), \(H(z)=1/\lambda>0\), and the objective is the same ratio.  The positive-denominator endpoint vertices found above map to feasible normalized optima, so unboundedness of \(\lambda\) when denominators approach zero does not prevent objective attainment.

We next establish scalar connectedness across orientations.  Let \(\mathcal D\) be the set of diagonal arrays satisfying the diagonal bounds, residual balance equations, and defier budget.  It is convex.  For \(d\in\mathcal D\), put
\[
 h_x^star(d)=\min\{U_x(d),V_x(d)\},\qquad
 H^star(d)=\sum_xh_x^star(d),\qquad
 B_x^star(d)=\min_kB_{xk}(d).
\]
The function \(H^star\) is concave because it is a sum of minima of two affine functions.  Hence
\(\mathcal D_+=\{d\in\mathcal D:H^star(d)>0\}\) is convex.

Starting from any feasible reduced point with \(H>0\), first move each \(n_x\), within its cut interval, to
\[
 n_x^ell(d,h)=\max\{0,h_x-B_x^star(d)\}.
\]
Then increase \(h_x\) linearly to \(h_x^star(d)\), retaining
\(n_x=n_x^ell(d,h)\).  The lower selection bound remains satisfied, the ordinal cuts remain satisfied by the ordinal-cuts lemma, and \(H\) stays positive.  Moreover the actual minority mass
\[
 \sum_x\bigl(\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x\bigr)
\]
decreases along this path, so the maintained budget continues to hold.  This connects the original point to the canonical point
\[
 \bigl(d,h^star(d),n^ell(d,h^star(d))\bigr).
\]
For two canonical points, join their diagonals by a line segment in \(\mathcal D_+\) and evaluate the same canonical formulas along it.  The functions involved are finite minima and maxima of affine functions, hence continuous; the resulting path remains feasible, has zero minority mass, and has positive \(H\).  The full positive-denominator reduced feasible set is therefore path connected.  By the projection--lifting theorem its ratio image is the causal identified set, and a continuous image of a path-connected set in \(\mathbb R\) is an interval.  The already-proved finite-branch endpoint attainment makes it the closed interval \([L,U]\).

Finally, the promised screen is observable and safe.  Write \((a)_+=\max\{a,0\}\), and define
\[
 \underline f_x=\max\left\{
  \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}(q^1_{x0w}-q^0_{x0w})_+,
  \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}(q^0_{x1w}-q^1_{x1w})_+
 \right\},
 \qquad
 \overline f_x=\min\left\{\sum_wq^1_{x0w},\sum_wq^0_{x1w}\right\}.
\]
The coordinate bounds for \(r\) imply
\(r_{xw}\in[(q^1_{x0w}-q^0_{x0w})_+,q^1_{x0w}]\), and the analogous bounds for \(s\) imply
\(s_{xw}\in[(q^0_{x1w}-q^1_{x1w})_+,q^0_{x1w}]\).  A box of coordinate intervals realizes every total between the sum of its lower endpoints and the sum of its upper endpoints.  Intersecting the two total intervals therefore proves that the exact pre-minority feasible range is
\(f_x\in[\underline f_x,\overline f_x]\).  Nonemptiness of the target implies
\(\sum_x\underline f_x\leq\delta_D\).  Consequently every feasible point obeys
\[
 f_x\leq \operatorname{cap}_x
 :=\min\left\{\overline f_x,
 \delta_D-\sum_{y\ne x}\underline f_y\right\}.
\]
Define the observable selected-state contrast
\[
 g_x=\sum_{i\in\mathcal Y}(q^0_{x0i}-q^1_{x0i})
     -\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y}(q^1_{x1j}-q^0_{x1j}).
\]
Direct substitution of the residual definitions gives
\[
 U_x-V_x=g_x+\sum_{i\in\mathcal Y}r_{xi}
                 -\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y}s_{xj},
 \qquad |U_x-V_x-g_x|\leq f_x.
\]
Thus \(g_x\geq\operatorname{cap}_x\) guarantees \(V_x\leq U_x\) at every feasible point, while
\(g_x\leq-\operatorname{cap}_x\) guarantees \(U_x\leq V_x\).  Fix the corresponding smaller-margin orientation in every such cell.  Dropping the other orientation loses nothing: its branch budget uses the larger nonnegative quantity and hence its feasible points are already feasible under the smaller-margin choice.  If \(r_{\rm amb}\) cells remain, there are at most \(2^{r_{\rm amb}}\) branches and two normalized endpoint programs per branch, or \(2^{r_{\rm amb}+1}\) programs.  Their coefficients are rational whenever the supplied masses and budgets are rational.

Use the full legal-arc representation constructed in the projection--lifting proof for one fixed orientation.  In each covariate cell it has \(2(K+1)\) left vertices and \(2(K+1)\) right vertices.  The row and column marginal equations have rank at most
\(4(K+1)-1\), because equality of the two total masses makes one equation redundant.  Across cells their rank is therefore at most
\[
 R_0=m\{4(K+1)-1\}.
\]
Apart from nonnegativity, this full-arc polytope adds only the defier-budget row and the orientation-specific minority-budget row.

Let a vertex have more than \(R_0+2\) positive arcs.  Restrict the marginal-equation matrix and the two budget rows to those positive columns.  There is then a nonzero vector \(\xi\) in their common nullspace.  For sufficiently small \(\epsilon>0\), both arc arrays \(a+\epsilon\xi\) and \(a-\epsilon\xi\) remain nonnegative, retain every marginal exactly, and retain the values of both budget left sides exactly.  They are distinct feasible points with midpoint \(a\), contradicting extremality.  Every vertex consequently has at most
\[
 m\{4(K+1)-1\}+2
\]
positive arcs.

The ratio argument in the attained-endpoints theorem applies to this compact full-arc polytope as well: every positive-denominator point is a denominator-weighted convex combination of its positive-denominator vertices.  Hence every finite lower or upper endpoint is attained at a positive-denominator full-arc vertex, and the displayed support bound applies.  Completing one response vector for each legal arc exactly as in the lifting proof gives a compatible full response law with no more support points than positive arcs.

For the stated extraction procedure, let \(t\) be a reduced optimum and lift one attaining reduced point to the corresponding full-arc branch.  At a lower endpoint, \(N-tH\geq0\) throughout that branch, including at \(H=0\) because then \(N=0\); hence \(N-tH=0\) exposes a face containing the lifted positive-\(H\) point.  At an upper endpoint the same assertion holds for \(tH-N\).  Maximize \(H\) over the relevant face and choose a vertex of the maximizing face.  Its \(H\) is positive, and a vertex of a face is a vertex of the original polytope.  The preceding rank argument therefore gives both the promised sparse law and an explicit finite LP extraction route.

Fix rational \(q\).  We give a finite exact construction; no output-sensitive complexity is asserted.  In each orientation eliminate a maximal fixed set of equality rows from its compact formulation and enumerate every subset of the remaining inequalities whose active normals can have full rank.  The entries of the constraint system are rational polynomials in \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\): \(\delta_D\) occurs only in the right side of the defier-budget row, and \(\delta_S\) occurs only in the coefficient row for the minority budget.  For any enumerated active set with nonzero determinant, Cramer's rule therefore expresses its candidate vertex coordinates as rational functions of the two budgets.  The corresponding \(N\), \(H\), and \(N/H\) are rational functions wherever \(H>0\).

These candidates cover every vertex at every parameter value.  Indeed, at a vertex the normals of its active constraints span the ambient space after the fixed equalities have been removed; selecting an independent spanning subset gives one of the enumerated determinants that is nonzero at that very parameter value.  Thus a determinant that vanishes on a boundary never licenses filling a value by continuity: a different nonvanishing active subset certifies every vertex that actually exists there.

Form a finite list of rational polynomials consisting of all candidate determinants, all numerators that test candidate feasibility and \(H>0\), all cross-products that compare two candidate ratios after their denominator signs have been recorded, and the polynomials defining the boundary of \(\mathcal B\).  Partition \(\mathcal B\) by the complete sign vector in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) of this finite list, discarding empty sign classes.  Each class is semialgebraic, the classes are disjoint and exhaustive, and zero signs retain determinant-zero, equality, boundary, and lower-dimensional pieces as separate strata.  On every class the feasible candidates, the positive-denominator candidates, and their weak ordering are fixed.  Therefore the global minimum and maximum are specified rational functions on every target-nonempty class; ties merely give two formulas with the same value.

The same finite tables are exact certificates.  A feasible vertex is certified by its active set, its rational coordinate formula, and the recorded slack signs.  If no branch has a feasible candidate, the table records, for every possible active basis, either a zero determinant or a violated constraint.  This certifies model infeasibility because any nonempty compact polytope has a vertex: minimizing a linear functional chosen outside the finitely many directions parallel to a positive-dimensional face gives one.  If feasible candidates exist but every one has \(H=0\), the table supplies a feasible model point and certifies target emptiness, because a nonnegative linear functional \(H\) has a positive value somewhere only if it has a positive value at a vertex.  Sparse full-law endpoint certificates then follow from the sparse-endpoint proposition.  This establishes the finite rational charts, all singular and lower-dimensional strata, and the two exact empty labels.

Let \(\delta'=(\delta'_D,\delta'_S)\) and \(\delta=(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) satisfy \(\delta'\leq\delta\) coordinatewise.  Every constraint other than the two budgets is unchanged.  Because \(f_x,c_x\geq0\), enlarging either budget weakens its corresponding inequality.  Hence
\[
 \bigcup_oQ_o(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_oQ_o(q;\delta_D,\delta_S),
\]
and, after restricting to \(H>0\),
\[
 \Theta_I(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 \subseteq
 \Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]
Suppose the target exists at \(\delta'\) and \(\delta\in\mathcal R_t\).  Endpoint attainment gives
\[
 L(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 =\min\Theta_I(q;\delta'_D,\delta'_S)
 \geq\min\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\geq t.
\]
Thus \(\delta'\in\mathcal R_t\), proving relative downward closure.  Requiring existence at the smaller pair is essential because compatibility itself expands, rather than contracts, with the budgets.

On each target-nonempty stratum supplied by the finite-rational-chart theorem, write \(L=A/B\) with the sign of the nonzero denominator \(B\) fixed.  The condition \(L\geq t\) is then one polynomial weak inequality, obtained by multiplying by the recorded sign of \(B\).  It follows that \(\mathcal R_t\) is a finite union of semialgebraic chart pieces.  Its boundary is contained in the finite union of chart boundaries and the algebraic equality pieces \(A-tB=0\), so it is finite piecewise algebraic.  The exact chart certificates distinguish: absence of every feasible branch, which is the falsification label; feasible branches with \(H=0\) at every vertex, which is the target-existence label; and positive-denominator pieces on which \(A-tB=0\), which is the conclusion label \(L=t\).  Intersections may carry more than one label, but the three causes are not conflated.

Put \(M_0=4m(K+1)\), and for observation \(i\) and multinomial category \(j\) let \(I_{ij}\) be its category indicator.  Then \(I_{1j},\ldots,I_{n_{\rm samp}j}\) are independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(\pi_j\), and \(\widehat\pi_j=n_{\rm samp}^{-1}\sum_iI_{ij}\).

For completeness, derive the needed Bernoulli tail bound.  If \(a>p\), then for every \(\lambda>0\), exponential Markov inequality and independence give
\[
 \Pr_p(\widehat p\geq a)
 \leq e^{-\lambda n_{\rm samp}a}
      \mathbb E_p\exp\left(\lambda\sum_i I_i\right)
 =\left[e^{-\lambda a}(1-p+pe^\lambda)\right]^{n_{\rm samp}}.
\]
For \(p<a<1\), differentiation gives the minimizing value
\(e^\lambda=a(1-p)/(p(1-a))\), and substitution yields
\[
 \Pr_p(\widehat p\geq a)
 \leq \exp\{-n_{\rm samp}D(a\Vert p)\},
 \qquad
 D(a\Vert p)=a\log\frac ap+(1-a)\log\frac{1-a}{1-p}.
\]
The boundary cases follow by limits.  As a function of \(a\),
\[
 \frac{\partial^2}{\partial a^2}D(a\Vert p)
 =\frac1{a(1-a)}\geq4,
 \qquad D(p\Vert p)=0,
 \qquad \left.\frac{\partial}{\partial a}D(a\Vert p)\right|_{a=p}=0.
\]
Twice integrating the second-derivative inequality yields
\(D(a\Vert p)\geq2(a-p)^2\).  The lower-tail calculation is identical.  Therefore, for every category,
\[
 P_\pi\bigl(|\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|>\varepsilon_n\bigr)
 \leq2\exp(-2n_{\rm samp}\varepsilon_n^2)
 =\frac{\alpha}{M_0}.
\]
No independence among the different category counts is used.  The union bound now gives
\[
 P_\pi\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq M_0}
 |\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|\leq\varepsilon_n\right)\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Since \(\pi\) lies in the simplex, the event in parentheses implies \(\pi\in\mathcal P_n\), proving primitive-region coverage.

On this single event, positive covariate masses and assignment overlap imply
\[
 \pi_{xz}=P(X=x,Z=z)>0
\]
for every \(x,z\), so the true arm-conditioning map is defined and the candidate \(\pi' =\pi\) is not omitted from the union defining \(\mathcal C_n\).  It follows deterministically, for every budget pair, that
\[
 \Theta_I(q(\pi);\delta_D,\delta_S)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_{\pi'\in\mathcal P_n}
 \Theta_I(q(\pi');\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\mathcal C_n(\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]
The projection--lifting theorem identifies the set on the left with the causal values among compatible full response laws.  Because the same primitive event was used for all budget pairs, the inclusion holds simultaneously on \(\mathcal B\), with no gridwise multiplicity step.  Restricting the statement to points where the population target exists merely excludes empty target sets and does not change the probability bound.

If \(\delta_D=0\), nonnegativity and \(\sum_xf_x\leq0\) imply \(f_x=0\) for every \(x\), so every compatible response law has no treatment defiers.  If also \(\delta_S=0\), then
\[
 0\geq\sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\}\geq0.
\]
Thus \(\min\{a_x,b_x\}=0\) in every cell: selection is one-sided within each covariate cell, although its direction may vary with \(x\).  Conversely, choosing in each cell the zero direction supplies an orientation branch with zero minority left side.  The branches therefore reduce exactly to the no-defier, covariate-dependent one-sided-selection model.

Under the additional premise that \(S_0=S_1=1\) almost surely among compliers, all complier mass is selected under both treatments.  Hence
\[
 U_x=V_x=h_x=c_x,\qquad H=\sum_xc_x.
\]
There are no missing complier margins to complete, and the ordinal-cuts lemma says that the attainable numerator is exactly the sharp ordered coupling range generated by the two complier outcome margins.  Projection--lifting proves that these and only these couplings correspond to full compatible laws, while attained connectedness turns their scalar image into the standard sharp interval.

For \(K=2\), the nonbenefit cuts are
\[
 B_{x,-1}=U_x,\qquad B_{x,0}=u_{x1}+v_{x0},\qquad B_{x,1}=V_x,
\]
and the benefit cuts are
\[
 G_{x,0}=v_{x1},\qquad G_{x,1}=u_{x0},\qquad G_{x,2}=U_x.
\]
Since \(h_x\leq U_x,V_x\), substitution into the exact cut interval gives
\[
 \max\{0,h_x-u_{x1}-v_{x0}\}
 \leq n_x\leq
 \min\{h_x,u_{x0},v_{x1}\},
\]
as claimed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every observed mass array \(q\) and budget pair \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B\), the projection onto \((d,h,n)\) of all laws \(P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) inducing \(q\) is exactly the \((d,h,n)\)-projection of \(\bigcup_{o\in\mathcal O}Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\).  Every full reduced array in every branch \(Q_o\) lifts to a full response law inducing the same \(q\), with the displayed \(h_x\) and \(n_x\).  Each branch admits a linear extended formulation with \(O(mK)\) variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients; its numerical coefficients are rational whenever \(q\), \(\delta_D\), and \(\delta_S\) are rational.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current equality is ill typed: its left side is projected onto \((d,h,n)\), whereas \(Q_o\) contains the full reduced array. The corrected statement applies the same projection to the union. It also makes the numerical rationality claim conditional on rational observed masses and budgets; arbitrary real probability inputs need not define a rational polytope.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: If \(\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) is nonempty, then it is the attained closed interval \([L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S),U(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)]\), even when the infimum of \(H\) over compatible positive-denominator laws is zero.  For each unscreened orientation having a positive-\(H\) feasible point, the two branch endpoints are obtained by the normalized programs in \(\mathrm{def:normalized\text{-}endpoint\text{-}program}\), and the same programs certify absence of a positive-\(H\) point otherwise.  After the observable residual-capacity direction screen, at most \(2^{r_{\rm amb}+1}\) linear programs are required.  These programs have rational data whenever \(q\), \(\delta_D\), and \(\delta_S\) are rational.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The geometric and linear-program claims hold for arbitrary real inputs, but an LP has rational data only when \(q\), \(\delta_D\), and \(\delta_S\) are rational. The proposed statement adds exactly that necessary qualification, restricts branch endpoints to branches with positive denominator, and records that infeasible normalized programs certify the other branches.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \(t\in[0,1]\), the robust region \(\mathcal R_t\) is relatively downward closed on its target-existence domain: whenever two budget pairs are coordinatewise ordered, the larger lies in \(\mathcal R_t\), and the target exists at the smaller, the smaller lies in \(\mathcal R_t\).  Whenever the fixed observed mass array is rational, the region has a finite piecewise-algebraic boundary obtained from the chart in \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}rational\text{-}charts}\).  The chart separately labels the falsification boundary, the positive-\(H\) target-existence boundary, and the conclusion boundary \(L=t\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Unconditional downward closure is false because lowering a budget can make the model infeasible or the positive-\(H\) target empty. For an explicit witness, take one cell with all units selected, complier mass \(0.4\), defier mass \(0.6\), and no same-treatment types. Its observed first stage is \(-0.2\), so the pair \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\) is infeasible, while at \((0.6,0)\) the target exists and belongs to \(\mathcal R_0\). The valid conclusion is downward closure relative to pairs at which the target exists; the finite-chart boundary clause also requires the rational-input premise of the theorem it invokes.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A completeness and bit-complexity proof for the degeneracy-safe adjacency-and-stratification algorithm \(\mathsf A_{\rm chart}\), including discovery of disconnected feasible chart components and canonical handling of singular and lower-dimensional ties.
open_obligations.obstruction: Finite active-set enumeration proves termination but can inspect exponentially many infeasible, singular, duplicate, or nonoptimal bases that emit no chart or certificate. No charging map from those rejected bases to the encoded output is available, and fixed-matrix parametric-LP arguments do not apply directly because the minority-budget row itself depends on \(\delta_S\).
open_obligations.attempted: The exact finite sign-stratification fallback, canonical active-basis certificates, determinant-zero strata, pointwise normalized LPs, and sparse full-law lifting were derived. Adjacency traversal was considered, but without a certified component-discovery mechanism and duplicate-work bound it does not establish the requested output-sensitive guarantee.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved finite fallback enumerates every orientation and every full-rank active set, retains zero-sign strata, compares all feasible positive-denominator vertex ratios exactly, and attaches active-set, emptiness, and sparse full-law certificates.  Pointwise endpoints require at most \(2^{r_{\rm amb}+1}\) rational linear programs for rational inputs.  What remains unproved is the stronger bound \(\operatorname{poly}(\ell_{\rm in},m,K)(M_{\rm out}+1)\): the fallback can inspect exponentially many singular, infeasible, duplicate, or nonoptimal active sets that produce no emitted chart.
